proposed.explanation:
Telecom Egypt's balance sheet is clearly getting stronger from FY2024 to FY2025. Total equity grew by roughly 38.6% (from 45,937,991,000 EGP to 63,687,826,000 EGP), while total liabilities grew only about 6.7% (from 152,014,797,000 EGP to 162,194,701,000 EGP). The debt-to-equity ratio improved from approximately 3.31 to 2.55, and the equity-to-assets ratio rose from about 23.2% to 28.2%. Cash and cash equivalents were stable at around 8.3 billion EGP. Total assets expanded 14.1%, driven primarily by the equity increase. All of these point to a strengthening capital structure, which aligns with your goal of owning solid companies over a 5-year horizon.

However, I cannot recommend a buy. Your current ETEL position (200 shares × 141.95 = 28,390 EGP) already represents 58.7% of your total portfolio value (28,390 + 20,000 cash = 48,390 EGP). The diversification rule requires that no single company exceed 50% of total portfolio value after a buy. Since ETEL is already above that threshold, purchasing any additional shares would worsen concentration and is not permitted. The best you can do right now is hold the existing 200 shares and keep your 20,000 EGP in cash until you have an opportunity to diversify into another company, which would bring ETEL back below the 50% cap and free up room to add more ETEL later if the balance-sheet trend continues.

Risks and caveats: The evidence covers only two balance-sheet dates and does not include income-statement data, cash-flow details, or segment-level information. A strengthening balance sheet is necessary but not sufficient for a 5-year investment thesis; earnings quality, competitive position, and regulatory environment also matter. The D/E ratio of 2.55, while improved, still indicates a leveraged company. This is guidance, not a guarantee of future performance.
